newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Car tariffs a security issue - Victoria state.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Car tariffs a security issue - Victoria state.

text.p: Australia's biggest car-making state, Victoria, condemned on Friday calls for Canberra to further slash tariffs on car imports and said car-making was strategically important to Australia's security.

Victoria Premier Jeff Kennett, whose government has warned that lower tariffs would destroy thousands of local jobs, said a heavy manufacturing base like car-making was crucial to the nation's long-term security.
"It also has huge ramifications for our defence capacity in years to come," he told state radio.

"I'm one of those who believe that we are not as a country secure for all time as a right and that if we ever have to defend ourselves then you need to have a heavy engineering capacity and that obviously can come from the automotive industry," he said.
Australia's Industry Commission handed down a draft report earlier on Friday recommending the national government cut car tariffs to five percent from the current 25 percent by 2004.
